Awesome, I was looking for a good article like this. Have you been to any of these places? If so, which ones were your favorites? Or just your favorite hiking spots in the area, in general.

Of the ones on that list, I've been to World's End, Spectacle Island, Halibut Point, Blue Hills Reservation, Breakheart Reservation, Middlesex Fells, and Noanet Woodlands. Also been to Wachusett Mountain, Walden Pond, Sandy Pond, Rocky Narrows Reservation, Broadmoor Wildlife Sanctuary, Moose Hill Wildlife Sanctuary... and a couple others whose names I can't remember.

I think Blue Hills is great - it has a nice mix of trails for all levels (from easy walking trails to more strenuous hikes), everything is really well-marked, it's free, and you can't beat the proximity to the city. This is probably my favorite of the local places. Middlesex Fells and Breakheart are pretty similar to Blue Hills, just a little bit smaller and maybe not as tough. Wachusett is great too if you can get out there. For interesting hikes, I like Spectacle Island and Halibut Point. Neither are really strenuous, but Spectacle Island is great for its views of Boston Harbor, and Halibut Point has an old rock quarry and huge slabs of rock right on the ocean.

The only one of those that I would avoid is Walden Pond. It might be worth the visit just to say that you've been there, but it's super crowded. Didn't really enjoy it at all.
Great insight, thanks! Does spectacle island tend to be very crowded? I feel like it would due to its location, but I actually haven't heard anyone talking about it before.

It's hard to say - I've only been there once. From what I remember though, most people were there for the beach, not the walking paths, so once I got away from that area, it was fine. If you're looking for complete solitude, this might not be the best place, but it didn't feel crowded at all to me. Seems like it would be a good place to bring friends/parents from out of town, as long as they don't mind taking a boat trip to get there and can handle some slight inclines.
